newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Pol Pot must be tried properly, says Albright.
newsitem.headline: Pol Pot must be tried properly, says Albright.

text.p: U.S. Secretary of State Madeleine Albright said on Tuesday Khmer Rouge leader Pol Pot was a war criminal who must face a trial that was internationally acceptable.

Albright told reporters she had not seen footage of a trial in the northern jungles of Cambodia at which the man widely detested for his role in the deaths of a million of his countrymen, was sentenced to life imprisonment.
"We don't know" what it all meant, she said.
"What we think is that it is very important that Pol Pot has to be tried. We consider him a war criminal and he must be tried by some procedure that is internationally accepted," she said.
Albright said U.S. officials were "exploring different ways to ensure that whatever trial there is, is appropriate, legal and valid in terms of the international community".
She declined to say what options they were pursuing.
Pol Pot, then known as "Brother Number One", led the Khmer Rouge into Phnom Penh in 1975, then emptied the populations of that and other Cambodian cities into the countryside.
By most reliable accounts, at least one million people died of disease, malnutrition and overwork or were executed as the Khmer Rouge tried to "cleanse" Cambodia of all but their views.
Footage of last week's jungle trial was shown on ABC-TV of the United States, which has exclusive rights to the video.

The apparent factional struggle within the Khmer Rouge which led to the trial was a factor in a coup in Phnom Penh earlier this month in which forces loyal to second prime minister Hun Sen ousted first prime minister Norodom Sihanouk.

The United States, at just-concluded meetings with other nations in Kuala Lumpur, put its weight behind an attempt by the Association of South East Asian Nations (ASEAN) to mediate an end to the Cambodian crisis.

Albright said that was the main topic of discussion of the meeting, which also included China, Japan, Russia, the European Union, Australia and India. ASEAN comprises Brunei, Burma, Indonesia, Laos, Malaysia, the Philippines, Singapore, Thailand and Vietnam.
Albright said the main focus would be to persuade Hun Sen to hold free and fair elections on schedule in May, 1998.

"I think we are building up leverage and the sense I got from the meeting, and the fact we spent so much time on Cambodia, was that there is a general sense that Hun Sen has to move towards credible elections, fair and free elections, in May '98," she said.
"We will keep our efforts focused on that," she added.
